## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sīlavattheragāthā* (Thag 12.1) is a poem located in the *Theragāthā* of the Pali Canon. The verses extol the supreme value and pervasive benefits of ethical conduct (*sīla*), describing virtue as bringing every manner of success (*sabbasampattiṃ upanāmeti*) [Keown 1992]. According to Damien Keown, the text and its commentary highlight a threefold happiness produced by morality—a good reputation, worldly goods, and rebirth in heaven or final nibbāna—while observing that the moral person (*sīlavā*) wins many friends [Keown 1992].
